title: Arabic bedroom labels
goal: A reader must be able to read the Arabic room and furniture labels naturally and identify the door, window, and dimensions of a small bedroom.

rubric.must: The Arabic room name and furniture labels read naturally from right to left, with the room name's words in the correct order and no reversed letters or mirrored glyphs.
Arabic letters use their normal contextual joined forms wherever Arabic spelling permits joining, with no words rendered as a sequence of isolated letters.
The Arabic room name fits inside the room, and all three Arabic furniture labels fit within their respective furniture outlines without clipping or overlapping symbol strokes.
The room has an Arabic bedroom name, and the bed, wardrobe, and table each carry the appropriate ordinary Arabic name for that object.
The drawing shows one rectangular room dimensioned 3 by 4 metres with exactly three furniture pieces, all inside its walls and clear of the door swing.
One door has a visible leaf and inward swing arc at a wall opening, and one window has visible glazing lines in a separate wall opening.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source and the rubric, without seeing the engine's own output. It preferred the svg: The SVG satisfies the Arabic typography, labeling, furniture-count, and opening requirements more closely than the picture.
